data.note:
Note: Compound unblinded as MG-132 (PubChem CID 462382, C26H41N3O5, BBBC021 structure agree; ChEMBL CHEMBL64925 with no curated mechanism, BBBC021 annotates as Protein degradation). My blinded conclusion of Microtubule stabilizers (p=0.89, e6-e9) was incorrect.

Reflection: MG-132 is a peptide aldehyde proteasome inhibitor (PMID:21499287, PMID:30695709) - expected Protein degradation phenotype. At 1 µM we saw enlarged cells/nuclei (e2) nearest to proteasome inhibitor I (similarity 0.751, e4), consistent. At 3 and 10 µM we saw extreme tub_mean z +54.7 and +116.4, tub_glcm_contrast z +151 and +328, high roundness/solidity and act_tub_ratio collapse (e6,e7) with NSC vote shifting to Microtubule stabilizers 2/4 and 7/10 neighbors docetaxel/epothilone/taxol similarity 0.845-0.915 (e8), plus Microscopist describing bright green tubulin bundles and mitotic rounding (e9). I weighted this high-similarity stabilizer signal over the single-well protein-degradation match and ignored high-dose toxicity/cell loss (39 and 14 cells vs 103 at 1µM, 410 debris objects at 30µM).

In retrospect, proteasome inhibition secondarily disrupts tubulin homeostasis, aggresome formation and mitotic progression, phenocopying stabilization at 24h in MCF-7. The dose-response was non-monotonic (tub_mean rho -0.20, p=0.8, e10) and low-dose profile already contained the true MoA signal. Lesson: at cytotoxic doses many classes converge on cytoskeletal collapse; orthogonal validation (pHH3, ubiquitin aggregates, proteasome activity) and weighting the low-dose, high-cell-count phenotype would have avoided over-calling Microtubule stabilizers.

reflection.text:
Retrospective reflection - MG-132 (PubChem CID 462382) - predicted Microtubule stabilizers p=0.89 vs true Protein degradation. Verdict incorrect.

What the data got right:
Initial sampling did NOT support a stabilizer. e2 (1 uM, n=103): cell_roundness z=-26.4, cell_solidity z=-26.3, cell_nuc_area_ratio z=+16.2 - loss of solidity/rounding with nuclear enlargement, not classic bundling. e3 (30 uM, n=410): nuc_solidity z=-414.8, nuc_form_factor z=-133.9, act_tub_ratio z=-159.3 - extreme nuclear dysmorphia/fragmentation and actin-tubulin imbalance. e4 compare_to_reference_atlas over 2 wells: Actin disruptors 1/2 NSC, k-neighbours Microtubule destabilizers 4/10, Epithelial 3/10, Actin disruptors 1/10 - stabilizers 0/10. Dose-response e10 over 4 wells: tub_mean Spearman rho=-0.20 p=0.8 - no monotonic tubulin increase expected for true stabilizer. And critically e8 over 4 wells did retain Protein degradation as 1/10 k-neighbours, and e4 early vote was also non-stabilizer.

What misled and why:
1. Measurements e6 and e7. Well w_b7bdfca819 3 uM (n=39) tub_glcm_contrast z=+151.7, tub_mean z=+54.7; w_5674222bb7 10 uM (n=14) tub_glcm_contrast z=+328.0, tub_mean z=+116.4. These very large positive z-scores for tubulin intensity/texture plus describe_phenotype e9 (6 observations, candidate: Microtubule stabilizers) created visual confirmation of bundling. This drove the reversal in e8 to NSC Microtubule stabilizers 2/4 and k-neighbours Microtubule stabilizers 7/10.

Why that was misleading: phenotype mimicry + acquisition bias. Proteasome inhibition by MG-132 is well established as Protein degradation/proteasome inhibitor mechanism PMID 21499287, PMID 30695709, PMID 21203833, PMID 18435911, PMID 36791578. Proteasome blockade causes accumulation of ubiquitinated/misfolded proteins, cell-cycle arrest, and apoptosis, which can produce increased tubulin texture, cell solidity increase (e6 z=+30.5), eccentricity loss (e7 z=-72.4), and apparent bundling/aggregation that is not direct microtubule stabilization. The e15 literature search returned 903 hits for 'MG-132 proteasome inhibitor mechanism', confirming this curated MoA, while e16 specific search for proteasome->microtubule stabilization returned 0 hits - we had no literature to support a mechanistic link and should have weighted that absence.

2. Comparison choice over-weighted. We upgraded hypotheses to 0.89 on e6/e7/e8/e9 and listed e3 as sole contradiction. In fact e3's 410-cell high-dose phenotype with massive nuclear solidity loss is more consistent with proteotoxic stress/apoptosis than stabilizer-induced mitotic arrest, and e4's early mixed vote already warned against premature stabilizer call. Review critique approved p=0.89 as calibrated citing concordance across two independent doses and explainable toxic drop at 30 uM, but concordance was between two low-N toxic wells, not independent replicates.

3. Acquisition choices amplified artifact. list_available_experiments e1 offered 8 doses 0.03-100 uM; we acquired only 4 wells, all single replicates, with a gap at the toxic end: 39 cells at 3 uM and only 14 cells at 10 uM. Z-scores inflate when computed on survivors with low N and selection bias. The non-significant dose_response e10 directly contradicted a dose-dependent stabilizer yet was ignored to submit conclusion. The 30 uM well retained 410 cells but with catastrophic nuclear features - not an empty well - suggesting late apoptotic/fragmented population rather than simple toxicity dropout.

If this were a real lab, orthogonal validation would have been required before p=0.89: proteasome activity (Suc-LLVY-AMC), ubiquitin conjugate western, and cell-cycle/pHH3 to distinguish proteotoxic G2/M delay from true microtubule stabilization and cold-stable microtubule assay vs docetaxel control, plus repeat with multiple replicates at non-toxic doses to test monotonicity. No clinical inference is made; this is screening assay interpretation only.
